title: Boss Case: The SHADOW42 Trail
subtitle: Combine everything you know to unmask the mastermind
conceptSummary: Real detective work combines SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, and LIMIT together in one query.

dialogue.text: This is it, Detective. All clues point to one customer who has been gaming our systems across multiple databases.
Find the customer with the most transactions, all completed, sorted by total spending. The top result is your suspect.
You'll need GROUP BY, COUNT, SUM, HAVING, and ORDER BY. Everything from World 2. This is the final exam.

teachMoment.title: Putting It All Together
teachMoment.body:
A complex query might look like this:

SELECT customer_id,
       COUNT(*) AS num_orders,
       SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent
FROM transactions
WHERE status = 'completed'
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 5

Every clause has a job. Together, they answer complex business questions.

task.instruction: Find the top 3 customers by total amount spent on completed transactions. Show customer_id, number of orders (as num_orders), and total_spent. Only include customers with 3 or more orders.

task.solution: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS num_orders, SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent FROM transactions WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3

winDialogue.text: Customer 206 — Farida Shaikh from Hyderabad! 15 total orders, highest lifetime spend. Cross-reference with SHADOW42 pizza orders: she's the connection!
Farida Shaikh. Gold loyalty member. Biggest spender. All those manipulated records trace back to her employee access credentials.
But she claims she was hacked. To prove it, we need to look at JOIN data from multiple tables. World 3 is calling...

storyBeat: CASE CRACKED — partially. Farida Shaikh's credentials were used. But was she the mastermind or a victim? The truth lies in JOIN queries across multiple tables. The real villain is still out there. World 3: The Join District awaits.
